title: Config-change-triggered tool eval orchestrator and arg validation shadow
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Background: When model variants or serving configuration change (quantization profile, kernel selection, routing rules, or version pins) we have observed silent regressions in tool/function selection and returned argument shapes. Existing regression gates primarily rely on bulk generation metrics and limited tool-specific suites. This ticket builds an orchestrator that automatically triggers targeted tool/function-calling evals whenever a config or model change is committed, runs them in a shadow mode, validates both selection accuracy and argument schema/semantic correctness, and produces a gating signal for rollouts and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: On merge of any config/model change (tags: model-version, quant-profile, routing-policy) the orchestrator queues a targeted eval job within 5 minutes
Targeted evals run in shadow (non-production) against a representative invocation dataset and complete within configured SLA (default 30 minutes for standard suite)

Selector accuracy and argument-validation metrics are computed and compared to a baseline; if any metric crosses the defined thresholds the system emits a regression alert to #invocation-regressions and creates a linear ticket automatically
Results stored in the console Eval dashboard with diffs against last-green baseline and an easy-to-read verdict (pass/warn/fail)
Canary vs global rollout policy integration: failing canary stops automated rollout and falls back to safe-model routing per policy
Unit and integration tests cover orchestrator job creation, queueing, runner idempotency, and a simulated failing-toolcase
plan: Phase 1: Build evaluator orchestrator service with lightweight trigger hooks for model/config changes (webhook + SCM watchers)
Phase 2: Implement shadow run mode that mirrors production routing but tags requests and isolates outputs for evaluation
Phase 3: Create tool-selection and arg-validation suites derived from existing human-annotated prompts + synthetic edge cases
Phase 4: Baseline computation, threshold configuration, and alerting rules wired to Slack and Linear
Phase 5: Console integration with a new Eval panel and rollout gating UI, plus doc for on-call/playbook
Phase 6: Gradual rollout behind a feature flag, monitor, iterate on false positives
metrics: false_positive_rate of alerts over first 2 weeks
time-to-detect (minutes) from config change to alert
rollouts: Enable orchestrator in dev orgs for first week
Shadow run for 100% of hosted API traffic for 2w with alerts muted (collect telemetry only)
Progress to canary enforcement for non-critical customers, then to stricter enforcement for enterprise orgs
Toggle in Console to pause automatic evals per-org for sensitive environments
